newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Polisario compares Morocco's actions to Iraq's.
newsitem.headline: Polisario compares Morocco's actions to Iraq's.

text.p: A leader of the Polisario Front, which seeks independence for Western Sahara, on Tuesday compared Morocco's role in the disputed territory to Iraqi designs on Kuwait.

Bachir Sayed, Polisario's "foreign minister", made the comparison in a letter congratulating former U.S. Secretary of State James Baker on his appointment on Monday as Secretary-General Kofi Annan's personal envoy for Western Sahara.
Baker played a key role in rallying the U.S.-led coalition which ejected invading Iraqi troops from Kuwait in 1991.

"There is no doubt that your immense prestige, credibility and moral integrity are bearers of hope and optimism for the Sahrawi people just as they were yesterday for Kuwait, another country like Western Sahara, which has a powerful 'brother' as its northern neighbour," Sayed wrote.

The United Nations, as part of a peace plan, has been trying for years to organise a referendum to decide whether Western Sahara should be incorporated into Morocco, which controls most of the former Spanish colony, or become independent.
Although a September 1991 ceasefire halted a brushfire war, the referendum has been repeatedly delayed because of differences over who should be eligible to vote.

Sayed, whose letter was circulated by Polisario's representative in New York, said Polisario was willing to cooperate with Baker's efforts "aimed at breaking the peace plan's prolonged deadlock and converting the fragile ceasefire between the Sahrawi and Moroccan armies into a just and lasting peace."

He said Baker knew well "the historic causes of this painful conflict and the principles and values at stake, not only for an innocent people, but also for the peace and stability of this highly sensistive region."
